title: Algebra Foundations
tagline: From your first variable to solving equations.

skills.title: Variables and notation
skills.objective: Read and write terms such as 4x, and simplify repeated letters.

skills.title: Substitution
skills.objective: Replace a letter with its value and work out the expression, including negative values.

skills.title: Like terms
skills.objective: Combine terms with the same letter by adding or subtracting their coefficients.

levels.title: Meet the Variables
levels.objective: Read and write terms such as 4x, and simplify repeated letters.

lesson.intro: A letter can stand for a number. It's called a variable.
steps: A variable is a letter, like x, that stands for a number.
4x means 4 × x. The 4 is the coefficient.
A number on its own, like 7, is a constant.
x + x + x is three lots of x, so it's 3x.
lesson.remember: Count the letters, and keep the letter.

levels.title: Substitute and Evaluate
levels.objective: Replace a letter with its value and work out the expression, including negative values.

lesson.intro: If you know what x is, you can work out any expression with x in it.
steps: Substituting means swapping a letter for its value.
Put the value in brackets: if x = 4, then 3x is 3(4).
Multiply before you add or subtract.
A negative value keeps its sign: if x = −2, then 3x = 3(−2) = −6.
lesson.remember: Brackets around the value keep the signs safe.

levels.title: Combine Like Terms
levels.objective: Combine terms with the same letter by adding or subtracting their coefficients.

lesson.intro: Terms with the same letter can be put together.
steps: Like terms have the same letters and powers, like 4a and 2a.
Add or subtract the numbers in front.
Keep the letter: 4a + 2a = 6a, not 6.
Unlike terms, like 4a and 2b, stay apart.

example.question: Simplify 5y + 4y − 2y
example.note: Each term keeps the sign in front of it.

lesson.remember: Same letter and power: combine. Different: leave them.

levels.title: Simplify Expressions
levels.objective: Simplify expressions with several letter and number terms, keeping each term's sign.

lesson.intro: Longer expressions simplify the same way, one kind of term at a time.
steps: Find the x terms and the number terms.
Each term takes the sign in front of it: −2x, +5.
Combine the x terms, then the numbers.
Write the x term first, then the number.

example.question: Simplify 4x + 3 − 2x + 5
example.note: The −2x moved with its minus sign.

lesson.remember: Move each term with its sign.

levels.title: Brackets and Common Factors
levels.objective: Expand a bracket by multiplying every term inside, and take out a common factor.

lesson.intro: A number outside a bracket multiplies everything inside it.
steps: Multiply every term inside: 3(x + 2) = 3x + 6.
Watch the signs: −2(x − 4) = −2x + 8.
Factorising goes the other way: find what every term shares.
6x + 9: both share 3, so 6x + 9 = 3(2x + 3).
lesson.remember: Multiply every term in the bracket, not just the first.

levels.title: Solve Linear Equations
levels.objective: Solve one- and two-step equations by doing the same to both sides.

lesson.intro: An equation says two sides are equal. Solving finds the x that makes it true.
steps: Do the same to both sides, so they stay equal.
Undo + 5 by subtracting 5.
Undo × 3 by dividing by 3.
Finish with x = a number, then check it in the original.
lesson.remember: Whatever you do to one side, do to the other.

levels.title: Algebra Adventure
levels.objective: Use everything from Algebra Foundations together, on your own.

lesson.intro: No new rules here: just you, your pencil and everything you've learned.
steps: Read each question: simplify, expand, factorise, work out or solve?
Work line by line, so Quack can follow you.
Check your answer by substituting when you can.

example.question: Simplify 2(x + 3) + 3(x − 1)
example.note: Expand both brackets, then combine like terms.

lesson.remember: One careful line at a time.
